# Sujātājātaka (Ja 306)

**ID:** Ja 306  
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Sujātājātaka  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul3.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul3.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sujātājātaka* (Ja 306), translated in English as *Queen Sujātā*, is a birth story in the Pali Jātaka collection. Set at Jetavana, its contextual frame narrative (*paccuppannavatthu*) concerns a domestic rift between King Pasenadi of Kosala and Queen Mallikā [Galasek 2016]. Following what the commentary terms a "bedroom quarrel" (*sayanakalaho*) or harem dispute regarding conjugal relations, the king refused to speak to Mallikā and treated her as though she did not exist, claiming that luxury and status had gone to her head [Nyanaponika et al. 2003; Galasek 2016]. When visiting the palace, the Buddha noted her absence, reminded the king that he himself had elevated Mallikā to her royal status, and praised the blessings of amity, successfully reconciling the royal couple [Nyanaponika et al. 2003; Galasek 2016]. To illustrate the folly of their friction, the Buddha related an incident from their past lives, introduced with the opening inquiry, "What is this egg-shaped fruit".

**Sources**

- [Nyanaponika et al. 2003] Nyanaponika Thera, Hellmuth Hecker, and Bhikkhu Bodhi, Great Disciples of the Buddha: Their Lives, Their Works, Their Legacy (2003) — Provided the narrative summary of the dispute between Pasenadi and Mallikā and the Buddha's intervention.
- [Galasek 2016] Bruno Galasek, On Presenting Characters and Representation of Persons... Characters in Narrative Suttas of the Majjhima Nikaya (2016) — Provided details on the nature of the dispute (sayanakalaho) in the paccuppannavatthu of Ja 306.
